steps.title: On the tray

steps.title: In your own time

steps.title: Nothing to decide

words.title: Start with the stone
words.text: Shape first, then size. We show you several side by side, loose and set.

words.title: Then the metal
words.text: Platinum, white, yellow or rose gold, against your own skin, by the window.

words.title: Then the band
words.text: Wedding bands made to sit flush beside the ring, or to stand apart from it.

engagementGuide.title: Choosing a ring
engagementGuide.intro: What we'd tell you across the tray, written down.

metals.title: Platinum
metals.text: White, heavy and dense. It wears to a soft sheen and holds a stone close.

metals.title: Yellow gold
metals.text: Warm against most skin. We work in 18ct for engagement rings.

metals.title: White gold
metals.text: The look of platinum at a lighter weight; it is plated and replated over the years.

metals.title: Rose gold
metals.text: Gold with a little copper. It flatters a pale stone and warms with wear.

settings.title: Claws
settings.text: Four or six. Six hold a round stone a little closer; four show more of it.

settings.title: Halo
settings.text: A ring of small stones around the centre. It makes the centre read larger.

settings.title: Bezel
settings.text: A rim of metal all the way round. Quiet, and kind to knitwear.

settings.title: Shoulders
settings.text: Plain, tapered or set with small stones, depending on the band it will sit beside.

engagementGuide.sizing: A ring should pass the knuckle with a little resistance and sit without turning. Fingers change with the weather and the time of day; we size in the afternoon, and resize once without charge in the first year.

weddingBands.title: Wedding bands
weddingBands.intro: Plain, brushed or set, made as a pair or to sit beside the ring you have.

notes.title: Width
notes.text: From 2 mm, which disappears beside an engagement ring, to 6 mm, which is a statement of its own.

notes.title: Profile
notes.text: Court (rounded inside and out), flat, or D-shape. We'll put each on your finger.

notes.title: Finish
notes.text: Polished, brushed or hammered. Brushed finishes soften over the years; we can refresh them.

notes.title: Fitted bands
notes.text: Shaped to sit flush against an engagement ring with no gap, made after we've seen the ring.

bespoke.title: Bespoke
bespoke.intro: Drawn for one person, made on our bench, from the first sketch to the last polish.
bespoke.timing: Most commissions take eight to twelve weeks from the first drawing.

photo.alt: Hands at a goldsmith's bench, a flame brought to a ring on the soldering block

steps.title: A conversation
steps.text: Bring photographs, a family stone, or nothing at all. We talk, and we draw.

steps.title: The drawing
steps.text: A finished drawing in pencil and wash, and the stones we'd suggest, loose on the tray.

steps.title: The model
steps.text: A model of the ring to try on, so the proportions are right before metal.

steps.title: The making
steps.text: Cast, set and finished by hand on our bench. We send photographs as it goes.

steps.title: Collection
steps.text: Upstairs, on the tray, in its box.

deposit.text: A deposit begins the drawing and secures the stones we choose together; the rest is due on collection. It is set against the price of the piece.

family.start: Send us a photograph and we'll tell you what can be kept. Then bring the piece in; nothing leaves your hands until you're happy with the drawing.

ringSizer.title: Ring size
ringSizer.intro: Three ways to find a size at home. We confirm it at your appointment either way.
ringSizer.postal: We'll post you a ring sizer, free, in a plain envelope. If it's a surprise, nobody needs to know what it is.
ringSizer.message: Hello Aldous Marr, could you post me a ring sizer, please? My address is:

aftercare.title: Aftercare
aftercare.intro: How to keep a piece as it left us, and when to bring it back.

items.title: Cleaning at home
items.text: Warm water, a drop of washing-up liquid and a soft toothbrush, then a lint-free cloth. Never for pearls: wipe them after wearing.

items.title: A yearly check
items.text: Claws wear. Once a year we clean your piece and check every setting, free, while you wait.

items.title: Resizing
items.text: Once in the first year without charge. Some bands can't be resized; we'll tell you before you buy.

items.title: Pearls
items.text: Last on, first off. Restring every few years if worn often; we'll look at the knots at your yearly check.

items.title: Repairs
items.text: Bring it in or post it to us, insured. We'll quote before any work.

items.title: Storage
items.text: Each piece in its own compartment, so stones don't scratch metal.

aftercare.reminder: Once a year, bring your piece in for a clean and a check of the claws and settings, free, while you wait.

anniversary.line: Add the date to your calendar, with time to choose. We never see it.

questions.a: Yes. Every visit is private: one table, one tray, and the pieces you asked to see. Request one here or on WhatsApp; we reply with times.
The door on Oyster Court is unmarked. Ring the bell under the monogram. Nobody else is shown in while you're with us.
Where we can. Pieces made to order or set with a particular stone say "Price on request", because the stone sets the price; we'll tell you on WhatsApp or at the table.
Most rings, yes, once in the first year without charge. Some bands, like full eternity rings, can't be; we say so before you buy.
Up to 24 letters inside any band we make, by hand, in about a week.

questions.q: Does it come in a box?
questions.a: Every piece leaves in our pale grey box, wrapped by hand, with a care card.

questions.q: How long does a commission take?
questions.a: Usually eight to twelve weeks from the first drawing. Tell us your date and we'll say honestly whether we can meet it.
Yes, £500 begins the drawing and secures the stones; it is set against the price.

questions.q: Do you clean and check pieces?
questions.a: Yes, free, once a year, while you wait. Add a reminder on the Aftercare page.
We can recommend an independent valuer; ask us at your appointment.
